t: K Items With the Maximum Sum — Tiered Greedy
o: Pick exactly k items from numOnes 1s, numZeros 0s, numNegOnes -1s to maximize the sum. Obviously take all available 1s first, then 0s as filler, and only dip into -1s if forced. Examples: k=2 with three 1s gives 2; k=4 gives 3+0 = 3.
k: Items have only three values, so the optimum is fully determined by how far k reaches through the tiers 1 -> 0 -> -1.
No sorting or data structures needed — pure arithmetic.

a.i: Take a = min(k, numOnes) ones. Subtract from k, consume up to numZeros zeros (worth nothing), then the remainder must come from -1s, reducing the sum.
a.t: O(1) — a handful of min operations.

a.i: Simulate picking items one at a time from the best remaining tier — equivalent, arguably more obviously correct, and easy to extend if item values change.
s: Loop k times: if numOnes > 0 take a 1; else if numZeros > 0 take a 0; else take a -1.
Accumulate the sum and return it.
a.t: O(k) — one iteration per picked item.

w: Give the O(1) formula; the loop is only a fallback. Pitfalls: forgetting that zeros absorb picks without changing the sum, and off-by-one when k exceeds numOnes + numZeros. Follow-up: items with arbitrary values (then it's just partial sorting / quickselect of the top k).
